title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Notation slip in (37): it mixes M̲(S) and 𝔊̲(A) and H_{S_0}(S). This is harmless (S = Spec A).

If M is genuinely profinite (the previous page says 'gr. pro (constants)'), M⊗_Z A needs a completed or continuous version. For instance, for A a Q-algebra and M = Ẑ the naive tensor product behaves badly (not zero, but huge). The page does not address this; presumably M is of finite type, or a completed tensor product is intended.

The margin's 'evidently trivial' torsor argument is correct. Each fibre torsor is the pushout of a constant M-torsor that has a section, namely a lift of h in 𝔊. So right exactness on sections holds for any S, not only affine S. This confirms Grothendieck's remark that the H^1 hypothesis is unnecessary.

ideas.what: Pushout of a group extension along an equivariant map of abelian kernels M → M⊗O, giving the group sheaf 𝔊̲ = 𝔊 ∧_M M̲.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of extensions / change of coefficients H^2(H,M) → H^2(H,M⊗A)
ideas.where_published: Similar constructions occur in SGA 3 / SGA 7 style group-sheaf formalism; this specific one is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Equivalence between data (M̲, 𝔊_{S_0} ⊃ M_{S_0}, hom, compatible action) and extensions 𝔊̲ ⊃ M̲ with Φ: 𝔊_{S_0} → 𝔊̲ inducing an iso on the quotients.
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the pushout extension (crossed-module/butterfly-type description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Giraud for non-abelian sheaf version
ideas.where_published: Refers to an internal §49 of the same manuscript.

ideas.what: Linearizing an extension of discrete/pro groups into an extension of a constant group by a vector group over a base ring, functorially in the extension.
ideas.modern_name: Akin to relative (Malcev/unipotent) completion of 𝔊 relative to 𝔊 → H, at the abelian first stage

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs, functorially in an extension 1 → M → 𝔊 → H → 1, the group sheaf 𝔊 ∧_M (M⊗O). This is an extension of the constant group H by the vector group M⊗G_a, apparently as a tool for the Galois–Teichmüller programme. It is in effect the first, abelian step of a relative unipotent completion of 𝔊 relative to H. Relative completion was later developed by Deligne and Hain and became a standard tool for mapping class groups and Galois actions.
missed.quote: une description "axiomatique" des extensions (35) en termes de (34)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck in the Longue Marche sequel moving toward algebraic-group (relative completion) models of extensions of fundamental groups. This is of modest historical interest; the mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful but standard pushout-of-extensions construction in sheaf language, with a routine exactness-on-sections check. Its only interest is historical context, as a possible precursor of relative-completion ideas.
transcription_corrections: The underlined 'G' is a Fraktur 𝔊 (as on the next page), and the map is Φ: 𝔊_{S_0} → 𝔊̲ (capital Phi). Later 'φ induit par φ' should read 'φ induit par Φ', and the operation is Θ (circled), 'déduite de Φ'.
'M_{S_0} [-...-] l'image inverse' is probably 'M_{S_0} = l'image inverse'.
'une description "...ique"' is likely 'et on a là une description "axiomatique"' (reading uncertain).
Before (37): 'pour tout schéma de base affine S' rather than ', sur H schéma de base affine S'; then 'on a une suite exacte'.
Under (37): '≃ M⊗_Z A' under M̲(S), '≃ H si S connexe' under H_{S_0}(S), and 'si S affine d'anneau A'.
Margin reads roughly: 'L'hypothèse affine sert de fait à assurer [H^1=0]... (plus généralement les M-torseurs sur S_0 définis par des images inverses... H... sont évidemment triviaux)'.
